title: Kernel prober and attention-burst harness for prefill/decode scheduling
creator: Asha Patel
description: Create a new benchmarking harness that probes kernel selection behavior under short attention bursts and staggered prefill/decode workloads. This ticket covers designing a micro-orchestrator that can replay mixed prefill+decode traces, inject attention pattern perturbations (burst/decay), and record deterministic kernel-routing decisions and per-token latency/cost. The goal is to detect regressions introduced by kernel-routing heuristics and attention optimizations and to provide stable golden baselines suitable for CI perf gates.
background: We have intermittent latency regressions in tail percentiles when models switch kernels mid-request due to attention window shifts or prefill concurrency. Existing bench suites focus on broad workload mixes but do not exercise short-lived attention bursts or staged prefill sequences that trigger kernel churn. This harness aims to fill that gap and give runtime teams a repeatable signal tied to kernel-selection correctness and scheduling trade-offs.
implementation_notes: Design a lightweight controller that can generate hybrid traces: sequences of prefill segments followed by multiple short decode bursts (1-20 tokens) to simulate chatty assistant workloads.
Implement an attention-pattern mutator that can create localized high-attention regions to force cache eviction / kernel fallback paths.
Capture kernel routing metadata at each step: selected kernel id, fallback reason, KV cache hit/miss, selected quantization path. Normalize into CSV for analysis.
Provide a deterministic mode that replays seeds with fixed scheduling to produce golden outputs; provide a randomized mode for fuzzing.
Integrate with the existing bench orchestrator but keep harness lightweight to run inside CI canaries with <2h runtime for full matrix runs.
Expose configuration knobs for batch size, concurrency, sequence length distribution, and prefill/decode gap timings.
Add an adapter that maps recorded live traces (from prod tail-capture) into harness-compatible episodes for regression repro.
Define a small canonical corpus of 24 episodes covering common and edge attention shapes; these form the initial golden suite.
Output artifacts: per-episode JSON metrics, kernel-transition timelines (CSV), profiler flame snapshots, and per-token cost breakdowns for console ingestion.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can run the canonical 24-episode suite end-to-end in deterministic mode and produce stable artifacts within a 5% variance window across 5 replays.
CI integration: a lightweight run (subsample of 6 episodes) executes in the CI perf job and fails when a defined perf gate threshold is crossed.
Recorded kernel routing telemetry includes kernel id and fallback reason at each token and is parsable by existing telemetry pipelines.
Docs: a short runbook describing how to add new episodes, interpret kernel-transition logs, and create/update golden baselines.
Owner acceptance: runtime lead signs off on the initial baseline and thresholds and the signal is used in at least one rollout canary.
test_plan: Unit tests for attention-pattern mutator and trace generator.
Deterministic replay test that asserts identical kernel-routing sequence across 3 replays in hermetic env.
Integration test that runs the subsampled CI suite and validates metric ingestion into bench dashboard.
Fuzz job that runs randomized episode variants overnight and records any kernel-routing anomalies for triage.
Manual review session with runtime and kernel teams to validate transition logs against local profiler snapshots.
